_comment: The shape `scripts/ingest-stock-data.mjs` reads out of data/robinhood-snapshot.json.
Generated by a session that can reach the Robinhood MCP — there is no script here,
because the MCP is reachable from an agent session and not from a shell, and no cron
can regenerate it. `robinhood_snapshot_fresh` is what makes that visible.
`positions` holds get_equity_positions verbatim, one call per account.
`lots[].lots` holds get_equity_tax_lots verbatim, ONE CALL PER SYMBOL PER ACCOUNT
(about 67 in total). Raw on purpose: the modelling lives in the ingest, so changing
how the data is shaped never costs another 67 calls.
If rate limits cut the pull short, record what was missed in `lotsUnavailable` and
leave the symbol out of `lots`. A short answer that reads as a complete one is the
one outcome to avoid; `robinhood_snapshot_lots_mapped` names the symbols that lack lots.
`orders` holds get_equity_orders verbatim, ONE PULL PER ACCOUNT: no `symbol` filter
(it can drop a fill with no error) and no `state` filter (a partly filled, then
cancelled order still moved shares). Follow `next` until it is empty and put every
page's orders in `items`. `createdAtGte` is the earliest newest-CSV date across the
accounts minus 7 days. Set `complete: true` only once pagination finished. The
ingest bridges only executions after each account's newest CSV row; see
